sources.used_for: Swan silhouette; rounded Say values: span 7.4 ft, wrist span 3.7 ft (50% of span), shoulder span 4 in, maximum body width 8 in, overall length 55 in. Paragraph wing area 6.61 square feet. The stated AR 8.29 is only a rounding cross-check: 7.4 squared / 6.61 is about 8.2844. Central planform is approximately parallel-chord with smoothly tapering outer panels.

Qualitative distinction between inner arm wing and outer hand wing; conventional tail, fin and rudder proposal. The model represents separate shoulder and wrist hinges, a horizontal tail and a distinct vertical fin/rudder. This page supplies no coefficients used in the benchmark.
Priority of the rounded Say column, required source separation, exclusions and warning that the historical notes are not a validated blueprint.

assumptions: Exact conversions: 1 ft = 0.3048 m; 1 in = 0.0254 m; square feet converted with 0.3048 squared. Individual exposed wing length = (span - shoulder_span)/2, not the inconsistent printed wing-length entry. Wrist and shoulder spans are full bilateral distances.
New task benchmark, not attributed to Stanley J. O. Tinn: mass 6 kg, gravity 9.80665 m/s^2, default density 1.225 kg/m^3; SI coordinates x forward, y up, z lateral.

The exact prescribed cycle-averaged polar is CL=clamp(0.6+3*alpha,-0.2,1.4), CD=0.035+CL^2/(pi*0.8*AR). Drag and thrust follow the relative-flow axis; lift is projected world-up rotated by roll. A projected lateral vector supplies the vertical-flow fallback.
New powered-drive assumption: 400 W mechanical input at full throttle and 65% propulsive efficiency; thrust 0.65*P/max(airspeed,5). This is not measured ornithopter performance.

New animation assumption: symmetric inner angle 0.42*sin(phase) radians; outer angle relative to inner 0.36*sin(phase-0.65) radians. Phase advances at 2 Hz whenever powered, independent of throttle magnitude, and freezes unpowered. Neutral phase retains the assumed wrist lag. Animation has no extra aerodynamic force contribution.

Visible wing chord is 12 inches in the central section, consistent with the Say average chord; outer chord tapers elliptically, with modest assumed aft sweep. Rounded feather marks, thickness, body cross sections, long neck, tail planform and fin shape are illustrative, not recovered engineering geometry.

Pitch-rate and bank controls, semi-implicit 1/120-second integration, point contact at y=0.2 m, support, 18 N maximum ground brake and touchdown limits are the new task specification. No imposed flight path, altitude lock, auto-level or hidden autopilot is present. Bank approaches the pilot's bank command as specified.
excluded_fields: Page 02 wing length 3.135 ft: inconsistent; instead derive each exposed wing from span and shoulder span.

Missing appendices, the distinct Standard Model Swan, and previous human-carrying simulators.
limitations: Educational approximation, not a physically validated aircraft or a flight-safety tool. Source photographs are historical observations and notes, not a complete blueprint.
Point-mass cycle-averaged dynamics: no unsteady flow, structural solution, aeroelasticity, wing inertia, stall hysteresis, ground effect or local wing-panel aerodynamics.
Articulated wings are independently animated for inspection; aerodynamic forces use a single constant reference area and the prescribed polar.
Tail and fin are visual conventional control surfaces; pitch and bank commands use the task's direct attitude-rate rules, not computed tail moments. No yaw/rudder actuation.
Ground contact applies to the point mass only; wings and tail have no individual collision constraints. Landing thresholds are simplified and crash damage is not simulated.
Any agreement with deterministic benchmark equations is not evidence of real-world flapping-flight performance.
